AGENDA

Council Chambers  Tuesday & Wednesday
City Hall  October 20 & 21, 2015
340 Palos Verdes Drive West  6:30 p.m.
Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities
Act. Please contact the City Clerk at (310) 378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to
request a disability-related modification or accommodation.

Any person who has made campaign contributions to any of the members of the Planning
Commission within twelve months before this meeting, should examine the provisions of
Government Code Section 84308 which is posted on the bulletin board outside the Council
Chamber.

We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign
contributions within the last twelve months.

The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after
the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City
Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerk’s office
(R05-14).

The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date
following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever
occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2)
Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend,
modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the
circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development
entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and
final.

The Planning Commission reserves the right to modify the order of items shown on the agenda and
advises all interested parties to arrive promptly at the commencement of the meeting.

MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  October 20, 2015

CALL TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 6:30 p.m. on October 20, 2015, in the City Council
Chambers, 340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of
Allegiance followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Absent:  None

Also Present: Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz;
  Assistant City Attorney John Cotti; City Clerk Vickie Kroneberger; Julie
  Cremeans, Minutes Secretary

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

John Dixon (641 Via Del Monte) came forward and expressed his opinion about the city as a
planned community and its intent to protect views.

CONSENT CALENDAR

1.  M-1047-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for a fence exceeding the
  allowable height at the single family residence located at 3409 Paseo Del Campo. Lot 15,
  Block 1612, Tract 6883. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California
  Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

  Applicant/Owner:  Laura Lamping

MOTION

  Commissioner Evans moved to approve M-1047-15 for 3409 Paseo Del Campo, exempt
from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0845
with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Welch and was carried by
unanimous oral vote.

Planning Commission  1  October 20 & 21, 2015
 OLD BUSINESS

3.  NC-1470R/M-1039-15; Consideration of Revised Neighborhood Compatibility &
  Miscellaneous Applications for the new single family residence located at 1120 Granvia
  Altamira. Lot 14, Block 1750, Tract 8652. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant:  Greg George
  318 Avenue I, #154
  Redondo Beach, CA 90277

Owner:  Ali & Karen Sarmast

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Evans asked about the status of the walls, and City Planner Corpuz advised that
there are still active permits and that there has not been a final resolution and is still being
addressed.

Commissioner Kao asked about the size of the trellis, and City Planner Corpuz advised that it is
proposed to be a 16.5 foot setback.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Greg George (2608 Coral Ridge Road, Rancho Palos Verdes) came forward and presented the
application.

Ian Hunter (2504 Novato Place) came forward to withdraw his letter in opposition to the original
proposal and commented that he and his wife are in favor of the new trellis system that was
approved by the Homes Association.

Julia Morita (1116 Granvia Altamira) came forward in support of the new trellis system and
expressed her concerns regarding the new concrete wall height.

Mr. George re-approached and addressed the concerns, stating that they will be taken care of,
pending final approval.

Commissioner Welch asked Mr. George about the 4.5 foot concrete wall height plan, and Mr.
George confirmed that it will go to 4.5 feet with the wrought iron.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Hunter commented that he is ready to approve, as his concerns have all been
addressed.

Commissioner Evans stated that he is in support of the new trellis plan, as it will reduce massing
and provide the right overall look, and is in supports of correct height on the walls.

Commissioners Kao and Welch and Chair Thomas also expressed their support of the
application.

Planning Commission  2  October 20 & 21, 2015
 MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve NC-1470R/M-1039-15 for 1120 Granvia Altamira,
exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-
0833 with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Hunter and was
carried by unanimous oral consent.

NEW BUSINESS

COMMISSIONER WELCH RECUSED HIMSELF FROM THIS AGENDA ITEM.

4.  M-1062-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for walls exceeding the
  allowable height within the setback adjacent to the street at the single family residence
  located at 449 Palos Verdes Drive West. Lot 22, Block 1514, Tract 6885. This project is
  exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3,
  Section 15303.

Applicant/Owner:  Tom Buttner
  Judco Partnership

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Tom Buttner (449 Palos Verdes Drive West) came forward and presented the application.

Chair Thomas asked Mr. Buttner about the purpose of the third step, and Mr. Buttner responded
that it prevents visibility into the new addition’s bathroom from the street.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Evans commented that he is very impressed by Mr. Buttner’s analysis of
surrounding properties, a number of properties in the have walls exceeding 6 feet in height, and
the applicant is concerned with safety and privacy.

Commissioner Kao agreed and added that neighborhood compatibility does not seem to be an
issue.

Commissioner Hunter explained that the examples cited as exceptions to the rule were beyond
the setback and not comparable and that it is important to maintain an open access and avoid
turning the city into neighborhoods of big walls along the street. The applicant is choosing to
push the limits and has alternatives.

Chair Thomas pointed out that the Commission has been directed by City Council to maintain an
open feel. However, every application has to be viewed on its own merits, and the applicant has
done just about everything to keep the impact minimal but still provide privacy. There may not
be a preponderance, but there are probably examples that do exist.

Planning Commission  3  October 20 & 21, 2015
 MOTION

  Commissioner Evans moved to approve M-1062-15 for 449 Palos Verdes Drive West,
exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-
0861 with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Kao and was
carried 3-1 with Commissioner Hunter dissenting.

COMMISSIONER WELCH RETURNED TO THE MEETING.

5.  NC-1541/G-1559/M-1053/M-1066-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 2812
  Victoria Place. Lot 16, Block 2450, Tract 7332. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant:  Rosa Velazquez
  118 S. Catalina Ave., #N
  Redondo Beach, CA 90277

Owner:  Ebrahim Soltani

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch asked about the notification process, and City Planner Corpuz explained
the process.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Rosa Velazquez (118 S. Catalina Avenue, Redondo Beach) came forward and presented the
application.

Ms. Velazquez commented that the neighbors to the north and to the south were concerned about
privacy and that the existing hedges and trees on the side of the house are being removed, except
for one tree.

Commissioner Kao asked about the trellis near the pool and the orientation of the windows, and
Ms. Velazquez explained the silhouetted trellis and the translucent windows and that the north
and south window orientation is a better approach for her because the ridgelines run in the same
direction.

Commissioner Hunter asked about the south side window, and Ms. Velazquez responded that it
is a combination, but that there are fixed windows on the second floor, south side.

Bizhan Khaleeli (27823 S. Montereina Drive, Rancho Palos Verdes, on behalf of the owner at
2806 Victoria Place), Jeanne Atamdede (2818 Victoria Place) and Fikret Atamdede (2818
Victoria Place) all came forward in opposition to the project due to privacy, view and noise
impacts and the looming nature of the gate, specifically pointing out the fire department’s brush
clearance program and the current drought conditions.

Ms. Velazquez re-approached and addressed the concerns raised, including the need for the
windows, the side yard, the vegetation, the small air conditioning unit, an existing wall.

Planning Commission  4  October 20 & 21, 2015
 Commissioner Hunter and City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz discussed the specific location of the
windows.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Hunter asked about the chimney regulations, the driveway width regulations and
the required setback line on the plan, and City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz provided details.

Commissioner Hunter discussed his concerns with the air conditioning unit, the windows, the
balcony, the chimneys and the trellis and asked that the applicant continue collaborating with the
adjacent neighbors to address the privacy concerns and reach a reasonable compromise.

Commissioner Evans agreed and added that if the magnificent greenery can be preserved it will
be nice for everybody, but if there is brush clearing that will be a serious consequence.

Commissioners Kao and Welch and Chair Thomas agreed.

CONTINUED TO THE NOVEMBER 17, 2015 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

6.  NC-1543/G-1560/M-1064/M-1065-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility,
  Grading & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 709
  Via Somonte. Lot 11, Block 1538, Tract 6884. This project is exempt from CEQA
  pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant/Owner:  GA Design Inc.

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Welch, Chair Thomas and City Planner Corpuz discussed the distance of the
required street setback.

Commissioner Kao and City Planner Corpuz discussed the maximum grading depth proposed.

Commissioner Hunter and City Planner Corpuz discussed the floor elevation proposed compared
to adjacent properties, and Commissioner Hunter stated that understanding the heights of the
homes across the street could be important in the evaluation of this proposal. City Planner
Corpuz advised that she will verify with a survey.

Commissioner Kao asked about deed restrictions, and City Planner Corpuz discussed the Code.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Mahmoud Garachedaghi (applicant at 709 Via Somonte) came forward and presented the
application.

Commissioner Welch asked the applicant what changes were made to the design after meeting
with the neighbors, and Mr. Garachedaghi responded that he discussed removing the roof deck
and the elevator shaft.

Ed Buchsbaum (777 Via Somonte), Steve O’Neil (712 Via Somonte), Rick Bohner (793 Via
Somonte), Elaine Bohner (793 Via Somonte), Derrek Lazzaro (804 Via Somonte), Cynthia

Planning Commission  5  October 20 & 21, 2015
 Lazzaro (804 Via Somonte), Vincent Jue (797 Via Somonte), John Dixon (641 Via Del Monte),
Essam Diebes (805 Via Somonte), Tracy Isenberg (1008 Via Nogales), Holly Nowzari (789 Via
Somonte), Vince Nelson (1629 Via Montemar), Dwight Streit (1641 Via Lazo), Ingrid Osborne
(828 Via Del Monte), Andrea Del Guercio (712 Via Del Monte), Richard Dennen (813 Via
Somonte), Ray Craemer (749 Via Somonte), Gerry Brooke (812 Via Somonte), Terry Pearson
(1505 Via Lazo), and Al Walsh (801 Via Somonte) all came forward in opposition to the project
due to privacy, view and massing impacts, the setting of a precedent, the lowering of property
values and Malaga Cove’s unique charm and distinct character.

Mr. Garachedaghi re-approached to address complaints and the speculation that someday
somebody else may build and reduce views and pointed out that future developers will have a
right to build, as long as they following the guidelines.

Commissioner Kao asked what Mr. Garachedaghi could do to bring the project down, and
Mr. Garachedaghi responded that it would eliminate his view from the main deck and that it is
not possible to excavate significantly in order to build this project.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Evans commented that there is more at stake here than the view impact to the Via
Somonte neighbors, that the mass is larger than what is allowed in many areas, that improving
the view is not even a starter until there is a reduction in the size and mass, and that the view is
severely impacted.

Commissioner Kao agreed and added that the view is significantly impacted, that the project is
unreasonable and has a very material impact to the Bohner residence, and that Malaga Cove is all
about the view, not lot sizes or big back yards.

Commissioner Welch also agreed and added that this property is a small and sloped lot, that
there are homes in Palos Verdes with similar layouts in order to gain the view, that the elevator
will allow access for many years, that the view impact could be quantified as 60%, that the
Bohners do have a large patio to take advantage of their views along their view corridor, and that
there are opportunities to reduce the size with reasonable impacts.

Commissioner Hunter commented that the Bohners have a massively expansive view, that the
loss of one narrow viewpoint is not a reasonable reaction, that the applicant has rights to build,
that it is difficult to balance the owner’s rights, the protection of the views and the compatibility
of the neighborhood, that it is not reasonable to ask the applicant to dig several feet into the
hillside, that neighborhood compatibility does not prohibit building two-story homes where
they’re permitted, and that the applicant should go back to the drawing board.

Commissioner Welch stated that the loss of downtown Los Angeles views should be considered
along with the loss of white water views.

Chair Thomas commented that this is not a vote of the neighborhood, that this is a situation
where the Commission objectively assesses whether impacts are reasonably and practicably
mitigated, that there is a lot of work to be done to mitigate the impact on the neighborhood, that
there is a high floor-area-ratio, that the whole size of the home probably needs to be reduced, that
it is not uncommon to require grading on an application like this, that it is a huge ask to try to put

Planning Commission  6  October 20 & 21, 2015
 two stories in the view corridor, and that the applicant deserves the opportunity to take another
shot at this.

CONTINUED TO THE NOVEMBER 17, 2015 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

7.  M-1048-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for a wall & accessory
  structure exceeding the allowable height within the setback adjacent to the street at the
  single family residence located at 2317 Via Pinale. Lot 4, Block 1620, Tract 6885. This
  project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14,
  Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant:  Resort Style Landscape
  20291 Oak St.
  Perris, CA 92570

Owner:  Eric Enriquez

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Kao asked about silhouetting, and City Planner Corpuz described the silhouetting.

Commissioner Welch asked whether the neighbor’s wall is permitted, and City Planner Corpuz
responded that she didn’t have that information.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Curt Chatwin (landscape architect at 20291 Oak Street, Perris) came forward and presented the
application.

Commissioner Welch asked about prohibiting people from falling down the 5 foot wall, and
Mr. Chapman responded that there will be plantings around the perimeter.

Commissioner Kao asked why the wall comes out farther then the neighbor’s, and Mr. Chapman
responded that the wall is in line with the neighbor but the street curves, so the proposal is to be
symmetrically set back from the curb, which puts it at a slight angle.

Commissioner Welch asked about Art Jury approval with his neighbor’s stone façade wall, and
Mr. Chapman responded that the finish matches the home, but a stone would make them look
like one wall.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman added that it is a tall wall that will require a barrier for safety
and that she would recommend allowing an additional 3 feet to maintain Building Code
requirements, and landscaping could be further conditioned to reduce the visual impact.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Welch asked that research be done regarding permitting of the neighbor’s wall,
and Commissioner Evans agreed. Commissioner Kao also agreed, adding that otherwise the
Planning Department would be looking to approve the neighbor’s fence as an after-the-fact
application.

Planning Commission  7  October 20 & 21, 2015
 Commissioner Hunter commented that it would be a 9 foot wall in the setback and that the
applicant was aware of the sloped lot when the property was purchased. Commissioner Hunter
further advised that although there is no benefit to the City to have such large setbacks, the
excessive setbacks have not been addressed, and the Commission has been directed not to
approve this type of application.

Commissioner Kao commented that it is within the Commission’s purview to condition a stone
wall to appear contiguous with neighbor’s property with parking a few yards away.

Chair Thomas advised that the concern with solid wall structures was to avoid a closed-in
feeling, but this is principally a retaining wall, so the home is not being walled in, and when
faced with lots with front and rear street frontage, the Commission has made exceptions to allow
the backyard to be functional.

Commissioner Hunter appreciated the distinction between a retaining wall and a wall that
encloses a space, but commented that there are other options to accommodate what the applicant
is trying to achieve; however, if there has been a consistent pattern in this circumstance and the
other adjacent property is approved and it is a retaining wall, as opposed to a fence, the
application can be supported.

CONTINUED TO THE OCTOBER 21, 2015 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

8.  M-1054-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 4008 Via
  Largavista. Lot 3, Block 6313, Tract 7143. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant
  to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant:  Mark Scott Associates
  2022 Orchard Dr.
  Newport Beach, CA 92660
